subject: Career
title: Job Crafting: Redesigning Your Role
description: A 60-second lesson on Job Crafting: Redesigning Your Role.

hook.text: She couldn't change her job. So she changed how she did it. Her satisfaction tripled without a title change.

buildup.text: Job crafting: proactively reshaping your tasks, relationships, or mindset within your existing role.

discovery.text: Wrzesniewski and Dutton found that even hospital cleaners who crafted their jobs reported higher purpose and satisfaction.

twist.text: You don't need permission to job craft. Volunteering for interesting projects or reframing tasks as meaningful — that's crafting.

climax.text: Three types: task crafting (what you do), relational crafting (who you work with), cognitive crafting (how you see it).

punchline.text: You can't always change your job. But you can always change how you do it.

quiz.question: What are the three types of job crafting?

details.summary: Job crafting is the practice of proactively reshaping your role by modifying tasks, relationships, or how you perceive your work. Unlike job design imposed by management, job crafting empowers employees to create more meaningful, engaging work within their existing positions.
details.whyItMatters: Job crafting is one of the most effective self-driven burnout interventions because it increases meaning and autonomy without requiring a job change. Research shows crafters report higher engagement and satisfaction.
takeaways: Job crafting modifies tasks, relationships, or cognitive framing
It increases engagement without requiring organizational permission
Even small role adjustments produce measurable satisfaction gains

faq.question: What are the three types of job crafting employees can practice?
faq.answer: Task crafting changes what you do by adding, removing, or modifying responsibilities. Relational crafting changes who you interact with by seeking mentors or collaborators. Cognitive crafting changes how you perceive your work by reframing tasks in terms of broader purpose or impact.

faq.question: Does job crafting require manager approval or organizational support?
faq.answer: Many forms of job crafting can begin without formal permission, especially cognitive and relational crafting. Task crafting may require conversation with managers, but framing changes as productivity improvements rather than personal preferences increases receptivity significantly.
